subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Pile Driving: Ancient Technique, Modern Scale
description: A fast breakdown of Pile Driving: Ancient Technique, Modern Scale for builders.

hook.text: Venice sits on millions of wooden piles driven into lagoon mud 1,000 years ago. They're still holding.

buildup.text: Piles transfer building loads deep underground. End-bearing piles rest on rock. Friction piles grip surrounding soil.

discovery.text: Modern impact hammers drive 30-meter steel piles in minutes. The vibrations can crack nearby buildings if miscalculated.

twist.text: Venice's wood piles survive because they're submerged. Underwater, without oxygen, wood doesn't rot.

climax.text: Bored piles drill and pour concrete in place. No vibration, no noise — perfect for tight city sites.

punchline.text: Pound it in or drill it down. Either way, the building stands.

quiz.question: Why haven't Venice's 1,000-year-old wooden piles rotted?
options: Salt in the lagoon water preserved the wood like a brine
Submerged in water without oxygen, wood doesn't decay
The specific tree species used is naturally rot-resistant
